objective_for_doctor: A 40-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have pain or weakness in your jaw, weakness in both arms and/or both legs, and previously, or do you currently, have any weakness/paralysis in one or more of your limbs or in your face.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve been having jaw weakness/pain, trouble swallowing, and my vision gets double. I also feel very short of breath, and I’ve had weakness in both my arms and legs, plus it’s hard for me to open or lift my eyelids. This has been going on before and it’s still happening.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—this sounds concerning for a neuromuscular problem like myasthenia gravis, but we need specifics: do you notice the symptoms are worse with activity and improve with rest, and do you have any fever or recent infection?  
Doctor: Also, when was the last time you were able to swallow liquids normally, and are you choking or unable to keep your head up?

Yes—my symptoms feel worse when I’m using my muscles, like talking, eating, and moving around, and they seem to get a bit better when I rest. I don’t have a fever, and I haven’t had any recent infection.  

I haven’t been able to swallow liquids normally for a while; I do have trouble with swallowing and I sometimes feel like I might choke. I can keep my head up, but it feels weak.

Doctor: This pattern (jaw/facial weakness, double vision, trouble swallowing, eyelids getting hard to open, and worsening with use) strongly suggests myasthenia gravis; I need to confirm timing and rule out urgent threats—do your symptoms improve after lying down or after taking a brief nap, and have you had any sudden breathing trouble, voice change, or inability to speak clearly?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Serum acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR Ab) and MuSK antibodies.

Yes, I think they get a little better when I lie down or after a rest/nap. I have had breathing trouble that feels worse over time, but I haven’t had a sudden one right at the moment. My voice can get weak, and I have trouble speaking clearly sometimes, but I’m still able to speak.

Doctor: This is highly consistent with myasthenia gravis with bulbar and respiratory involvement; I’d like to confirm severity—right now, can you count to 20 out loud in one breath, and are you able to swallow your own saliva without choking?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Serum acetylcholinesterase (if available) + CBC/CMP + TSH; also REQUEST TEST: Chest CT (or CT chest) for thymoma and REQUEST TEST: Bedside spirometry/forced vital capacity (FVC) to assess respiratory risk.
I can’t reliably count to 20 in one breath right now—I start running out of air and my voice gets weaker. And swallowing my own saliva is hard; I sometimes feel like I might choke.

Doctor: You’re describing significant respiratory/bulbar weakness—can you take a deep breath and tell me if you can blow out a candle / say “one Mississippi” repeatedly without your voice fading, and do you feel any chest tightness or are you working harder to breathe at rest?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Bedside Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) / Negative Inspiratory Force (NIF) now; also REQUEST TEST: ABG/VBG and pulse oximetry.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Urgent neurology consult and start NPO—do you have any past history of autoimmune disease or thymectomy/thymoma, and are you currently on any medications that can worsen neuromuscular transmission (e.g., beta-blockers, magnesium, fluoroquinolones, macrolides)?

I can try, but my voice fades and I get short of breath when I talk for more than a few seconds. I don’t know about the candle test exactly, but I do feel like I’m working harder to breathe even when I’m resting, and there is some chest tightness.  

I don’t know of any autoimmune disease history, and I haven’t had a thymectomy. I’m not sure what medications I’ve taken recently—I can tell you what I have if you want to check the list.

Doctor: This is a medical emergency—your inability to sustain speech, saliva-related choking, and breathing effort with chest tightness suggest myasthenic crisis. While you provide your medication list, I need immediate objective respiratory measures: can you let me get an urgent bedside FVC/NIF right now, and do you have a pulse oximeter reading?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Immediate bedside Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) and Negative Inspiratory Force (NIF) now; REQUEST TEST: Pulse oximetry + ABG/VBG; REQUEST TEST: Chest CT (if not already) to assess for thymoma.

I’m here, doctor, but I can’t do the breathing tests well right now—my voice and breathing get worse quickly if I try to do deep breaths or speak for long. I don’t have a pulse oximeter reading that I can see.

Doctor: With rapidly worsening voice and breathing plus saliva/choking difficulty, I’m treating this as **myasthenic crisis** even without FVC/NIF yet—are you able to speak in full sentences right now, or do you feel unable to swallow or breathe safely?  
Doctor: Do you have any “rescue” inhalers or oxygen at home, and can you tell me your current medication list (especially antibiotics like azithromycin/fluoroquinolones, magnesium, beta-blockers)?

I can speak, but only for short parts of sentences before my voice gets weak. I feel like I can’t swallow safely—sometimes I feel like I’m going to choke—and breathing feels difficult.  

I don’t have a rescue inhaler or oxygen at home. I’m not sure of every medication name right now, but if you want, tell me the ones you’re worried about and I can check whether I’ve taken any recently.

Doctor: Your symptoms are severe right now—speaking only in short sentence fragments, poor saliva swallowing/choking sensation, and worsening breathing strongly indicate **myasthenic crisis with impending respiratory failure**; we can’t delay.  
Doctor: I’m going to treat this as an emergency: **DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenic crisis (bulbar/respiratory myasthenia gravis)** — please get you to the ER/ICU immediately for airway monitoring and start appropriate therapies.

[DDX]
1. Myasthenia gravis
